title: A microwave assisted method to synthesize nanoCoFe2O4@methyl cellulose as a novel metal-organic framework for antibiotic degradation
author: Nasiri, Tamaddon, et al.
materials: MC, CoCl2·6H2O, NaOH, and FeCl3·6H2O were obtained from Merck Company (Germany) and used without further purification. MNZ with a purity of 99% was purchased from Tamad Pharmaceutical Company (Tehran, Iran). Other chemicals such as HCl, NaOH, acetonitrile, acetic acid, methanol, and ethanol were obtained from Merck Company (Germany). All the materials were in analytical grade and used without further purification. Deionized water was used to make solutions.

Dark brown solutions were subjected to microwave irradiation (3 × 5 min at 450 W) (Samsung Microwave ME201, 20 L). Afterwards, nanoCoFe2O4@MC was precipitated as a lightweight massive powder. The obtained magnetic solids were separated by using an external magnet and then washed with deionized water many times. Afterwards, they were dried at 100 °C in a vacuum oven for 24 h [11] (Fig. 2). The Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) of the samples was obtained using a FT-IR 6300 Brucker, and the X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) of nanoCoFe2O4@MC was recorded in the diffraction angle range of 2θ = 10○–80○ by an X'Pert PRO MPD PAnalytical using Ni-filtered Cu Kα radiation. Thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA), derivative thermogravimetric analysis (DTG), and differential thermal analysis (DTA) were carried out using an STA (PC Luxx 409-NETZSCH) instrument at the rate of 10 °C min−1 in air. steps.title: Gather chemicals and equipment
steps.instruction: Obtain methyl cellulose (MC), CoCl2·6H2O, FeCl3·6H2O, NaOH, HCl, acetonitrile, acetic acid, methanol, ethanol, and metronidazole (MNZ, 99 % purity) from Merck (Germany) or Tamad (Iran); use deionized water for all solutions; have a Samsung ME201 microwave (20 L, 450 W), external magnet, vacuum oven, FT‑IR, XRD, TGA, VSM, FE‑SEM‑EDS, BET analyzer, UV‑Vis DRS, flame AAS (λ = 240.7 nm Fe, 248.3 nm Co), HPLC (Waters YL‑9100), Plexiglas batch photoreactor (25 × 10 × 5 cm, 300 mL), three 6 W low‑pressure UV‑C lamps, peristaltic pump (1 mL s⁻¹), and alcohol for washing.

steps.title: Dissolve metal salts
steps.instruction: Weigh FeCl3·6H2O and CoCl2·6H2O in a 2:1 molar ratio, add them to 50 mL deionized water, and stir until completely dissolved at room temperature.

steps.title: Add methyl cellulose and stir
steps.instruction: Introduce the required amount of MC to the metal‑salt solution and stir vigorously at room temperature to obtain a homogeneous suspension.

steps.title: Adjust pH to 13
steps.instruction: Within 1 hour add aqueous NaOH solution dropwise while monitoring pH until the suspension reaches pH 13.

steps.title: Microwave‑assisted synthesis
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to the Samsung ME201 microwave and irradiate three successive cycles of 5 min each at 450 W (total 15 min).

substeps.instruction: Place the reaction vessel in the microwave.
Run the first 5‑min cycle at 450 W.
Allow brief cooling (≈1 min) and repeat for the second and third cycles.

steps.title: Collect and wash product
steps.instruction: Allow the reaction mixture to cool, then use an external magnet to separate the lightweight brown nanoCoFe2O4@MC powder; wash the magnetic solid repeatedly with deionized water until the wash water is clear.

steps.title: Dry the nanocomposite
steps.instruction: Place the washed nanoCoFe2O4@MC in a vacuum oven set to 100 °C and dry for 24 h.

steps.title: Prepare photoreactor
steps.instruction: Assemble the Plexiglas batch reactor (internal dimensions 25 cm × 10 cm × 5 cm, volume 300 mL) with three 6 W low‑pressure UV‑C lamps mounted on the top; connect a peristaltic pump delivering 1 mL s⁻¹ to ensure mixing.

steps.title: Prepare MNZ solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve MNZ in deionized water to obtain the desired initial concentration (e.g., 5 mg L⁻¹ for optimal tests); adjust the solution pH to the target value (e.g., pH 11) using HCl or NaOH.

steps.title: Add catalyst and start irradiation
steps.instruction: Add the required amount of dried nanoCoFe2O4@MC to the MNZ solution (e.g., 0.2 g for 300 mL, corresponding to 0.67 g L⁻¹); immediately start UV‑C irradiation and the peristaltic pump.

substeps.instruction: Ensure uniform suspension of the catalyst.
Set irradiation time according to the experimental plan (e.g., 120 min for optimal condition).

steps.title: Sample at defined times
steps.instruction: At predetermined intervals (e.g., every 15 min), withdraw an aliquot, separate the catalyst magnetically, and store the clear supernatant for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze MNZ by HPLC
steps.instruction: Inject 20 µL of each filtered sample into the HPLC equipped with a C18 column (5 µm, 250 mm × 4.6 mm); use a mobile phase of acetonitrile : water (30 : 70 v/v) at 1 mL min⁻¹; detect at 348 nm; calculate removal efficiency η = 100 (C₀ − C_t)/C₀.

steps.title: Recycle catalyst
steps.instruction: After each run, separate the nanoCoFe2O4@MC with a magnet, wash it with an alcohol/water mixture, and dry at 100 °C; then reuse the recovered catalyst in a fresh MNZ solution under the same UV‑C conditions for subsequent runs (up to at least four cycles).

steps.title: Check metal leaching (optional)
steps.instruction: Collect the reaction supernatant after the fourth run and determine Fe and Co concentrations using flame atomic absorption spectroscopy at 240.7 nm (Fe) and 248.3 nm (Co) to confirm chemical stability.
